papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: The authors use a structure-based drug discovery pipeline to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein, a mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. This offers a potential new therapeutic angle against SARS-CoV-2 that may be less vulnerable to resistance mutations in existing drug targets.

papers.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to predict how Xiaojin Pill, a traditional Chinese medicine, might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks of combining it with sorafenib. The work is largely computational and predictive, offering hypotheses about mechanisms and combination safety rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
papers.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes for the many Golgi-associated proteins whose assemblies remain uncharacterized, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (like catalytic residues and domains) rather than diluting signals across whole-protein embeddings. This avoids the need for accurate 3D structures, making EC number prediction more broadly applicable than structure-based approaches.

papers.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
papers.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint takes a family-level structural clustering approach across 1.89 million clusters from the AFESM database to profile taxonomic composition, rather than starting from individual Asgard proteins. The analysis identifies candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and reveals a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds across the tree of life. This expands the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins in Asgard archaea and highlights structural clustering as a complementary strategy for deep homology detection.

papers.title: Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.
papers.abstract: A series of thirteen 1-(benzyloxy)-2-phenyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole derivatives was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as α-glucosidase inhibitors. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the presence of a chlorine atom at the C-6 position of the benzimidazole core, combined with suitable substituents on the pendant aromatic rings, was associated with relevant α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Among the series, compounds 6 and 13 emerged as the most potent derivatives showing IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM, respectively, and greater potency than acarbose (IC50 = 139 μM) un
papers.summary: The authors synthesized thirteen benzimidazole derivatives and tested them as inhibitors of α-glucosidase, an enzyme targeted in diabetes management. Two compounds (6 and 13) inhibited the enzyme more potently than the standard drug acarbose, with compound 13 being roughly nine-fold more potent, and kinetic studies indicated an uncompetitive inhibition mechanism. Computational docking and modeling supported the structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.
papers.abstract: Changes in bile acids (BAs) balance lead to various metabolic diseases, yet current treatment options targeting these changes remain severely limited. CYP8B1 (cytochrome P450, family 8, subfamily B, polypeptide 1) is a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls the synthesis of 12α-hydroxylated (12α-OH) BAs. Inhibiting CYP8B1 is an attractive therapeutic strategy for attenuating 12α-OH BA levels, remodeling the gut microbiota and thereby ameliorating metabolic diseases. CYP8B1-specific inhibitors are currently lacking due to structural similarities between the active site of CYP8B1 and other CYPs, a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors report the development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors, a liver enzyme that produces 12α-hydroxylated bile acids implicated in metabolic disease. Selectivity is challenging because CYP8B1's active site resembles those of other cytochrome P450 enzymes, but these compounds aim to lower 12α-OH bile acids and remodel the gut microbiota as a therapeutic strategy. This is an early-stage drug discovery effort toward a previously untargetable metabolic target.

papers.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-provided distance constraints (e.g., from crosslinking or FRET experiments) into AlphaFold-Multimer to improve protein complex structure prediction. The method addresses cases where standard predictors fail to correctly assemble complexes despite available experimental distance information, offering a multi-step approach to integrate these constraints.

papers.title: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.
papers.abstract: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin-like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well-tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand-bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower-angle rotameric state, while T195
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational energetics of serine versus threonine at position 195 in thrombin, a key catalytic residue in trypsin-like serine proteases. The authors find distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes for S195 and T195 in both apo and ligand-bound states, with S195 favoring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state. The work provides a molecular-level explanation for the strong evolutionary preference for serine over threonine at this catalytic position.

papers.title: Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graph attention networks (GATs) are emerging as powerful aritficial intelligence (AI) tools for learning biomolecular dynamics, yet extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention remains challenging. Here, we present an interpretable AI approach that combines molecular dynamics prediction with mechanistic interpretation through attention-derived communication networks. We develop three edge-aware GAT models - Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, and Edge-Gated - that differ in how edge information is incorporated during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, our edge-aware models impr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce three edge-aware graph attention network variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, and show they outperform a standard GAT. They then use the learned attention weights to construct communication networks that offer mechanistic interpretation of the underlying biophysics. This provides a framework for combining predictive modeling with interpretable mechanistic insight.

papers.title: Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.
papers.abstract: Biased agonism at the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) offers a promising strategy for developing safer cardiovascular therapeutics. While β-arrestin-biased agonism has been extensively investigated, G protein-biased signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we report structures of AT1R coupled to G protein and either the endogenous agonist angiotensin II (AngII) or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar overall poses, with coordinated rearrangements extending from the orthosteric pocket to the intracellular surface. The structures provide a detailed view of a TM7
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports cryo-EM structures of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) bound to G protein with either the natural agonist angiotensin II or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The two ligands bind in similar poses but trigger coordinated structural rearrangements that propagate from the binding pocket to the intracellular surface, revealing how biased signaling is encoded structurally. These findings offer a template for designing safer cardiovascular drugs that selectively activate G protein pathways.

papers.title: A computational-experimental strategy identifies K-7174 against African swine fever.
papers.abstract: African swine fever (ASF), caused by the African swine fever virus (ASFV), poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production due to the absence of effective vaccines or therapeutics. Targeting the virally encoded RNA polymerase (RNAP), which is essential for viral transcription, offers a promising antiviral strategy. Capitalizing on our previously resolved high-resolution structure of ASFV RNAP, we conducted a rigorous structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries (T001 and LF1000) to identify selective inhibitors. From 100 candidates validated in vitro, nine compounds ident
papers.summary: The authors used the high-resolution structure of the African swine fever virus RNA polymerase to perform structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries, identifying nine candidate inhibitors after in vitro validation. One compound, K-7174, emerged as a promising antiviral hit against ASF, demonstrating a computational-experimental pipeline for antiviral discovery.

papers.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
papers.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r
papers.summary: The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the African swine fever virus E2 enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experimentally confirmed the I215L–FAM105A interaction, and structural analyses characterized the binding interface. This suggests FAM105A as a potential host factor in ASFV replication and a possible antiviral target.

papers.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s
papers.summary: The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with machine learning to engineer enzymes for better utilization of biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors like NMNH, which are cheaper alternatives to natural cofactors such as NADPH. This addresses the poor activity natural enzymes typically show with these alternative cofactors, offering a computational alternative to directed evolution and rational design. The approach aims to lower synthesis costs in biocatalysis by enabling more efficient cofactor use.

papers.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.
papers.summary: This study identifies bisphenol PH as a high-risk endocrine-disrupting chemical that impairs ovarian function by disrupting and downregulating the LHCGR gene, a key receptor for luteinizing hormone. The authors also propose a prioritization framework for ranking bisphenol analogs by their ovarian toxicity risk and molecular initiating events.

papers.title: The evolutionary history of transporters of the plastid outer envelope of Chloroplastida- a structure-sequence comparison.
papers.abstract: Plant metabolism heavily relies on plastids, derived from once free-living organisms. However, how two distinct organisms merged into one remains currently only partially understood. Protein-mediated metabolite exchange across the double-membrane plastid envelope is essential for plant cell function. Here, we investigate the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) involved in these transport processes. The mosaic nature of the nuclear genome and the deep evolutionary distance since plastid acquisition are major challenges. To address them, we combine sequence-based analy
papers.summary: This study investigates the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) that mediate metabolite transport between the plastid and the rest of the plant cell. By combining sequence-based analyses with structural comparisons, the authors trace the evolutionary history of these transporters across Chloroplastida, shedding light on how the ancestral endosymbiont's transport machinery was repurposed during plastid acquisition. The work helps clarify the mosaic evolutionary origins of proteins central to plant metabolism.

papers.title: Thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazones as selective prostate cancer agents: biological profiling and molecular targeting studies.
papers.abstract: A series of thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazone derivatives 5a-5t was synthesized and evaluated for anticancer activity using biological and computational methods. The cytotoxic activity of these compounds was tested on A549, LNCaP, and HUVEC cell lines utilizing the MTT assay, with sorafenib used as a control drug. The activity of the derivatives was shown to be cell line- and substituent-dependent, with the highest cytotoxicity against LNCaP cells. Compound 5d, bearing a 2,3-dichlorophenyl group, was the most potent derivative against LNCaP cells (IC50 = 2.50 µM; SI
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazone derivatives and tested them against lung cancer (A549), prostate cancer (LNCaP), and normal endothelial (HUVEC) cell lines. Compound 5d, with a 2,3-dichlorophenyl substituent, was the most potent and selective against prostate cancer cells (IC50 = 2.50 µM), and computational docking studies were used to explore its molecular targets. The work identifies a promising scaffold for further development of selective prostate cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences.
papers.summary: GPCRAgent is a multi-agent platform that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to support GPCR-targeted drug discovery. It addresses the limitations of standalone LLMs by integrating structured domain knowledge, aiming to improve interpretability and systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions.

papers.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
papers.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify existing drugs ebastine and ceritinib as inhibitors of FtsZ, an essential cell-division protein in the cancer-associated bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum. These compounds could serve as starting points for antimicrobials aimed at reducing F. nucleatum enrichment in colorectal cancer tissues. The work is preliminary, with activity likely demonstrated in vitro and further validation needed.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine synthetic metal cofactors with protein scaffolds to enable reactions not found in nature. It focuses on how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs), incorporated via genetic code expansion, can bridge natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry, expanding the chemical diversity available for catalysis. The authors survey strategies for integrating ncAAs and synthetic cofactors to design new catalytic functions.

papers.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct
papers.summary: DeepEST is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts Gene Ontology terms for bacterial proteins by combining gene expression, gene location, and predicted protein structure data. This approach addresses the large fraction of bacterial proteins that remain functionally uncharacterized, potentially improving annotation and understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms.

papers.title: The evolutionary conserved protein-RNA interface formed by the cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C.
papers.abstract: Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) is an essential cell-fate regulator that guides the animal body plan during early development and maintains organ homeostasis in adults. It does so by binding specific mRNA targets and regulating their translation, yet the molecular basis of mRNA target selection has remained unclear. Here, we combined experimental and computational approaches to define the Bicc1-RNA interaction. In vitro binding experiments with wild-type and mutant RNA substrates identified the RNA features recognized by Bicc1, while protein-RNA XL-MS-a UV-crosslinking approach coupled to LC-MS/MS-pinpoint
papers.summary: This study defines the molecular basis by which the cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) selects its mRNA targets, combining in vitro binding assays with mutant RNA substrates and protein-RNA crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS). The authors identify specific RNA features recognized by Bicc1 and map the protein-RNA interface, revealing an evolutionarily conserved interaction mechanism underlying translational control during development and adult tissue homeostasis.

papers.title: Acetyl tributyl citrate induces neuronal ferroptosis through ATM-associated disruption of iron and redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is widely used as a non-phthalate plasticizer, raising concerns about its potential health effects. Although emerging evidence suggests that ATBC may adversely affect the nervous system, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given the critical role of ferroptosis in neuronal injury, this study investigated whether ferroptosis contributes to ATBC-induced neuronal injury and explored the potential involvement of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) in this process.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the common non-phthalate plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) harms neurons by triggering ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death. The authors link ATBC exposure to disruption of iron and redox homeostasis via the ATM protein, suggesting a mechanistic pathway for ATBC neurotoxicity. The work adds to concerns about the safety of this widely used plasticizer.

papers.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven protein design has moved beyond structure prediction to actively creating new enzymes, using the vast uncharacterised microbial sequence space as both a source of raw material and a testing ground. It surveys three stages: mining microbial sequence space, generative design of novel biocatalysts, and the broader shift from predicting to creating enzyme function. The authors frame the 2021 structure-prediction breakthrough as the inflection point that enabled these organism-agnostic design tools.

papers.title: BioLiP3: a protein-ligand affinity database integrating curated data with LLM-enabled literature mining.
papers.abstract: Quantitative binding affinities and three-dimensional protein-ligand structures provide complementary information essential for structure-based drug discovery, yet these data remain largely disconnected across existing databases and the biomedical literature. We present BioLiP3, a major extension of BioLiP that expands quantitative affinity coverage 13-fold within its structure-centered framework for biologically relevant interactions. BioLiP3 contains 593 423 affinity records, of which 591 820 are linked to three-dimensional protein-ligand structures: 45 386 experimentally resolved PDB comple
papers.summary: BioLiP3 is a major expansion of the BioLiP database that integrates quantitative protein-ligand binding affinities with three-dimensional structural data, growing affinity coverage 13-fold to nearly 600,000 records, most of which are linked to experimentally resolved PDB structures. The authors also use large language models to mine the biomedical literature for affinity data, helping bridge the gap between scattered affinity measurements and structural databases. This provides a unified resource for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an
papers.summary: The authors identify and characterize the first meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from an archaeon (Pyrococcus sp.), an enzyme that uses NADH or NADPH to stereoselectively aminate α-keto acids into D-amino acids. This expands the limited toolkit of stable, D-stereoselective dehydrogenases useful for biocatalytic production of D-amino acids with coenzyme recycling.

papers.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
papers.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was pe
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening and affinity-based methods to search for small molecules that bind conserved regions of the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD outside the shallow ACE2-binding interface, aiming to block the RBD-ACE2 interaction that mediates viral entry. This explores alternative druggable pockets on the RBD as a strategy for antiviral small-molecule discovery.

papers.title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR.
papers.abstract: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This paper presents a set of calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein, using dedicated NMR experiments to obtain atom-resolved information on protein–ligand interactions. The work aims to establish a rational design framework for drugs targeting intrinsically disordered proteins, which lack fixed structures and are difficult to drug conventionally.

papers.title: From molecular pathways to nanocarrier design: a translational framework for lipid-based nanoparticles in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease, being a complicated neurodegenerative disoder affects cognitive as well as memory functions. Characterised by amyloid-β aggregation, along with tau hyperphosphorylation, and cholinergic dysfunction, this disease is also associated with oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Conventional clinical interventions, like acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and novel monoclonal antibodies predominantly rely on symptomatic alleviation of symptoms. Nevertheless, these conventional treatments come across considerable constraints, like temporary effectiveness, lesser therapeutic reach d
papers.summary: This review proposes a translational framework linking Alzheimer's disease molecular pathways (amyloid-β aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, cholinergic dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation) to the rational design of lipid-based nanocarriers for drug delivery. It argues that conventional therapies like acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and monoclonal antibodies offer only symptomatic relief with limited brain penetration, and that nanocarrier engineering guided by disease biology could improve therapeutic targeting and efficacy.

papers.title: Structural basis for saccharide binding by human RNase 2/EDN: Insights into its potential lectin-like properties.
papers.abstract: Human RNase 2, also named the eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN), is a secretory protein of the vertebrate-specific RNase A superfamily involved in antiviral and proinflammatory cell response. Identifying ligand-binding pockets in EDN is thus relevant to structure-based drug design. By X-ray crystallography we first identified a conserved site at the protein surface binding to carboxylic anion molecules: malonate, tartrate and citrate. Searching for potential biomolecules rich in anion groups and considering previous report of EDN interaction to glycosaminoglycans, we explored the protein bin
papers.summary: This study used X-ray crystallography to identify a conserved surface pocket on human RNase 2/EDN that binds carboxylic anions like malonate, tartrate, and citrate. Building on prior evidence of EDN-glycosaminoglycan interactions, the authors explored saccharide binding, revealing potential lectin-like properties of this secretory protein. These structural insights could inform structure-based drug design targeting EDN's ligand-binding pockets.

papers.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en
papers.summary: Poké is a new computational tool that identifies ligandable pockets on protein surfaces by combining energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score. It works on both static protein structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics trajectories, making it useful for detecting cryptic sites that only appear after conformational changes. The tool aims to be fast and reliable for structure-based drug design applications.

papers.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.
papers.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing e
papers.summary: This Account describes a multi-disciplinary effort to validate the enterovirus 2C protein as a drug target, moving beyond phenotypic screening by rationally optimizing quinoline-based inhibitors originally found in a drug-repurposing campaign. The work yielded compounds with improved potency and selectivity against EV-D68 and integrated resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development to support 2C-targeted antiviral discovery.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities are being extended beyond structure determination to ligand-target recognition, addressing the bottleneck of limited structural information on pharmacological targets for natural products. It highlights applications to complex natural products including bioactive peptides, proteinaceous compounds, and molecular glues, where structural knowledge is critical for mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization in drug discovery.

papers.title: HEDGEHOG: hierarchical evaluation of drug generators through rigorous filtration.
papers.abstract: Generative molecular models can support early drug discovery by proposing new candidate compounds de novo. In practice, useful candidates must balance target-relevant activity, physicochemical properties, and other multiparameter design constraints. However, standard metrics commonly used to evaluate molecular generators only weakly reflect whether the generated compounds are medicinally plausible and suitable for downstream computation. This can produce an incomplete view of model performance and inefficient use of computational resources. We introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evalu
papers.summary: The authors introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evaluation pipeline for generative molecular models used in drug discovery. It filters generated compounds through successive criteria reflecting medicinal plausibility and downstream computational suitability, addressing the weakness of standard metrics that poorly capture practical utility. This provides a more rigorous, multiparameter assessment of model performance.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of novel BCL-XL inhibitors through molecular docking and key interaction-guided virtual screening.
papers.abstract: BCL-XL, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 protein family, is an attractive therapeutic target for overcoming apoptosis resistance in cancer. However, the large, shallow, and predominantly hydrophobic nature of its BH3-binding groove has complicated the discovery of potent, drug-like small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we employed structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to identify novel BCL-XL inhibitor scaffolds with relatively low molecular weights (MWs). Approximately 312,000 drug-like compounds were docked into the BH3-binding groove, and the top-ranked molecule
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to dock ~312,000 drug-like compounds against the BH3-binding groove of BCL-XL, aiming to find novel low-molecular-weight inhibitor scaffolds. The study addresses the challenge of targeting BCL-XL's large, shallow, hydrophobic binding pocket and reports top-ranked candidate molecules from the screen.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that integrates predictive models from multiple member databases to classify protein sequences into families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring broad coverage of UniProtKB and linking to resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe.

papers.title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study tested five psychotropic drugs (aripiprazole, fluoxetine, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate) for their ability to inhibit glutathione S-transferase (GST), an enzyme involved in detoxification and tumor drug resistance. Using in vitro enzyme kinetics with equine liver GST and molecular docking, the authors characterized inhibition patterns and identified interactions that could inform repurposing of these drugs as GST inhibitors in cancer therapy.

papers.title: From "undruggable" to tractable: Therapeutic advances targeting Kristen rat sarcoma viral homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C)-mutant cancers and emerging resistance mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This review explains the evolution of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C) from an "undruggable" target to a manageable oncogenic driver in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While first-generation inhibitors have significantly improved patient care, the emergence of complex resistance mechanisms necessitates a shift toward precision-driven combination therapies and advanced computational drug discovery. The KRAS G12C mutation is a primary driver in approximately 8.9% of NSCLC patients, particularly smokers. The development of covalen
papers.summary: This review traces how KRAS G12C, once considered undruggable, became a targetable oncogenic driver in NSCLC, with first-generation covalent inhibitors improving patient outcomes. It highlights emerging resistance mechanisms and argues for precision combination therapies and computational drug discovery to sustain clinical benefit.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: This study uses cryo-EM to determine the high-resolution structure of podophage A1002, which infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The authors identify 11 structural proteins and describe a novel split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fiber architecture in the phage tail, providing a structural basis for engineering phage-based antimicrobials.

papers.title: Molecular force gates regulate mechanical transmission across the nuclear envelope.
papers.abstract: The LINC (linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton) complex is a central mechanotransductive apparatus that physically couples cytoskeletal forces to the nuclear interior, thereby regulating nuclear architecture, chromatin organization, and downstream signaling. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we identify and characterize 'force gates' within the LINC complex - structural interactions that maintain mechanical connectivity under load. By introducing targeted mutations into the KASH peptide and SUN protein, we provide computational evidence that a key disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563
papers.summary: Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, the authors identify 'force gates' in the LINC complex—specific structural interactions, including a SUN2 disulfide bond (Cys563), that maintain mechanical connectivity between the cytoskeleton and nuclear interior under load. Targeted mutations in the KASH peptide and SUN protein computationally disrupt these gates, suggesting they regulate force transmission across the nuclear envelope.

papers.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba
papers.summary: The authors show that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about multiple protein conformations, even when a single structure is output. By analyzing these distributions, they develop a method to predict an alternative conformation of a known protein structure. This suggests that standard AF2 predictions harbor underexploited multi-state structural information.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
papers.abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology combined with experimental validation to identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid formation. The authors integrate toxicogenomic and keloid-associated gene networks to prioritize VCAM1, then validate its differential expression experimentally. The work suggests a possible environmental exposure contribution to keloid pathogenesis, though the evidence is preliminary.

papers.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.
papers.summary: This study profiles the N-glycoproteome in a mouse model of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), a chronic lung disease of preterm infants marked by arrested alveolarization. The authors identify aberrant N-glycosylation of integrin beta-1 (ITGB1), suggesting a link between glycosylation-dependent ECM-receptor signaling and impaired lung development. The work provides a first N-glycoproteomic landscape for BPD and nominates ITGB1 glycosylation as a candidate pathogenic mechanism.

papers.title: Apigenin Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Endothelial Activation and Injury-Associated Phenotypes in Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells.
papers.abstract: Sepsis represents a severe challenge in critical‑care medicine. Protecting endothelial function and alleviating microvascular inflammation and oxidative stress help reduce sepsis‑associated mortality. Apigenin, a natural flavonoid, exerts anti‑inflammatory and anti‑oxidant effects; its mechanisms against endothelial injury relevant to sepsis remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether apigenin, a natural flavonoid, can protect human umbilical vein endothelial cells from lipopolysaccharide-induced activation and injury phenotypes relevant to sepsis. The findings suggest apigenin attenuates endothelial activation and injury-associated phenotypes, supporting its potential as an anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agent in sepsis-related endothelial dysfunction.

papers.title: Enhancing the flexibility of the peripheral regions within the catalytic cavity of a family 5 glycoside hydrolase CelB for improving catalytic efficiency.
papers.abstract: Glycoside Hydrolase family 5 (GH5) endoglucanases are indispensable biocatalysts in lignocellulosic biorefining and their intrinsic catalytic performances play vital roles in process economics and enable broader industrial applicability. Herein, we engineered the catalytic domain of a bi-modular GH5 endoglucanase CelB from Bacillus sp. Strain N-4 by targeting non-conserved residues around peripheral, solvent-exposed regions. The site-specific mutagenesis identified two single-point mutants Y40G and T177N, which exhibited 1.64- and 1.55-fold increases in specific activity, respectively. Molecul
papers.summary: The authors engineered a GH5 endoglucanase (CelB) by mutating non-conserved residues at the periphery of the catalytic cavity, identifying two single mutants (Y40G and T177N) with ~1.5-1.6-fold higher specific activity. The work suggests that increasing flexibility in solvent-exposed peripheral regions can improve catalytic efficiency, offering a generalizable protein-engineering strategy for cellulases.

papers.title: Clinical characterization and in silico structural analysis of microtubule-related gene variants in eleven patients.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze associations of Microtubules (MTs) mutations with nervous system phenotypes, summarize mutation characteristics of genes including TUBA1A, TUBB2A, TUBB4A, and TUBGCP6, explore clinical phenotypic diversity and molecular mechanisms, and expand the MTs genotype-phenotype spectrum.
papers.summary: This study characterizes microtubule-related gene variants (TUBA1A, TUBB2A, TUBB4A, TUBGCP6) in eleven patients with nervous system phenotypes and uses in silico structural analysis to explore how the mutations may affect protein function. The work expands the known genotype-phenotype spectrum for microtubule-related neurological disorders.

papers.title: Microcystin-LR exposure induces cartilage degeneration and dysregulates osteoarthritis-associated targets: an integrative computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Microcystin-LR (MC-LR), a prevalent cyanotoxin in eutrophic freshwater, is becoming a more widespread environmental contaminant as global warming promotes cyanobacterial blooms, and its health effects may extend beyond its well-documented hepatotoxicity.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether microcystin-LR, a common cyanobacterial toxin, can damage cartilage and contribute to osteoarthritis. Using both computational target prediction and experimental validation, the authors show that MC-LR exposure induces cartilage degeneration and disrupts genes and pathways linked to osteoarthritis.

papers.title: Olanzapine induces Mdivi-1-resistant disruption of insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells.
papers.abstract: Second-generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine (OLZ) are widely prescribed because they produce fewer extrapyramidal adverse effects than first-generation agents. However, OLZ is strongly associated with metabolic dysfunction, and alterations in mitochondrial dynamics have been proposed to contribute to these effects. We investigated whether OLZ-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to impaired insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells and explored a potential interaction with the mitochondrial fission regulator dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1).
papers.summary: This study shows that the antipsychotic olanzapine disrupts insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells through mitochondrial dysfunction, and that this effect cannot be rescued by Mdivi-1, a DRP1 inhibitor. The findings suggest olanzapine's metabolic side effects involve mitochondrial dynamics but through mechanisms that bypass or resist DRP1 inhibition.

papers.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses suggest a myeloid-associated candidate role of THBS1 in sepsis.
papers.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of mortality worldwide, and biomarkers that integrate inflammatory dysregulation, immune-cell localization, and prognostic relevance remain limited. To identify a candidate molecule linked to myeloid immune responses in sepsis, we performed an integrated analysis of public bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing data, a small exploratory clinical RNA-sequencing cohort, and compound screening analyses.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from public datasets and a small clinical cohort to identify THBS1 as a myeloid-associated candidate gene in sepsis. The findings suggest THBS1 may serve as a biomarker linking inflammatory dysregulation and immune-cell localization, though validation remains exploratory.

papers.title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations of DOCK2 associated with early-onset recurrent infections.
papers.abstract: Dedicator of cytokinesis 2 (DOCK2) deficiency is a rare combined immunodeficiency characterized by defects in both cellular and humoral immunity and caused by pathogenic mutations in the DOCK2 gene. Herein, we report a 3-year-8-month-old Chinese girl presenting with recurrent infections, immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), elevated IgE levels, and a hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)-like episode to broaden the clinical phenotype spectrum of the DOCK2 defect.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 3-year-old Chinese girl with a rare DOCK2 deficiency caused by novel compound heterozygous mutations. She presented with recurrent infections, immune thrombocytopenia, elevated IgE, and an HLH-like episode, expanding the known clinical spectrum of this combined immunodeficiency.

papers.title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics and machine learning to identify candidate diagnostic biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) that are linked to neuroinflammation-related gene programs. The authors frame the work as hypothesis-generating, aiming to uncover molecular connections between liver disease and neuroinflammation. Specific biomarker candidates and validation results are not detailed in the abstract.

papers.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.
papers.summary: This study identifies carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) as a key regulator that restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis. The findings suggest CA4 could serve as a molecular target for diagnosing and treating this severe, often irreversible drug toxicity.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens ebelin lactone, a triterpenoid derived from bacosides, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including targets involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. The work extends prior findings of its binding to M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors by profiling its structural compatibility across a broader set of cognition-associated proteins. It is a purely in silico docking/structural analysis without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa.
papers.summary: This study integrates pharmacological and experimental validation to show that the natural isoflavone Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 in prostate cancer cells, which alters ROS/STAT3 signaling and reprograms chemokine expression to modulate the immune microenvironment. The authors propose GSTM2 and downstream chemokine pathways as candidate targets for addressing biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach
papers.summary: This study uses multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations to predict how mutations at the IL-17A–IL-17RA protein interface perturb the structure and dynamics of the complex. The authors aim to identify mutations that disrupt the interaction, which could inform therapeutic strategies for inflammatory autoimmune diseases targeting this signaling axis. The work is a computational, simulation-based analysis rather than an experimental validation study.

papers.title: A Tanshinone IIA Sulfonate Derivative Targets USP21 to Induce SCD1 Degradation, Suppressing NSCLC Metabolism and Enhancing Antitumor Immunity.
papers.abstract: Background: The deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 21 (USP21) is a key regulator of tumor metabolism and immune homeostasis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Its aberrant activation drives malignant growth, metabolic reprogramming and immune resistance, yet specific USP21 inhibitors for NSCLC therapy remain scarce. We aimed to develop a selective USP21 inhibitor, define its immunometabolic mechanism, and validate its anti-tumor and immunotherapy-sensitizing effects in NSCLC. Methods: We performed structure-based hierarchical virtual screening of a Food and Drug Administration (FD
papers.summary: This study identifies a Tanshinone IIA sulfonate derivative as a selective inhibitor of the deubiquitinase USP21 in non-small cell lung cancer. The compound induces degradation of SCD1, disrupting tumor lipid metabolism and enhancing antitumor immune responses, suggesting a potential immunometabolic therapeutic strategy for NSCLC.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer, then tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways in a diabetic-mimetic CRC model. Hupehenine suppressed tumor cell phenotypes and altered macrophage marker profiles, suggesting it may target the diabetes–cancer interface. The work is preliminary but points to a potential therapeutic angle for diabetic CRC patients.
